title: Homogeneous fractions lift with every denominator formula
statement: Let k be a field, S=k[x0,x1] with its standard grading [def-sc-p1-standard], P=Proj S, G an O_P-module and M a Z-graded S-module with additive pieces M_z and S_n M_z contained in M_(n+z). Let phi_z be additive equivalences M_z -> Gamma(P,G tensor O_P(z)) for z>=0, compatible with homogeneous multiplication [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. For f in S_d, define Rel(x,s) to mean that some m>=0 and y in M_(m*d) satisfy x=y/f^m in M_f and that phi_(m*d)(y) restricts to multiplication of s by f^m on D+(f). Assume d>0, G coherent [pqf-def-coherent], M internally graded and M_z=0 for z<0. For every x in degreeZeroFractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions], there is s with Rel(x,s) such that, for every m and y in M_(m*d), x=y/f^m implies the displayed restriction formula for y and s.

source.place: Proposition 0BXD, final paragraph; parent chart proof step 1

proof.text: Normalize a degree-zero fraction to y/f^m with y in M_(m*d). If f=0, LocalizedModule.subsingleton applies because 0 belongs to powers(f); choose m=0 and y=0. Otherwise unpack degreeZeroFractions and the powers-submonoid witness. The denominator f^m is nonzero, and MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.inj_right identifies its two degrees. This is the proved private helper fraction_power_rep.

Multiplication by f^m is bijective on G-sections of D+(f). First D+(f) is contained in D+(f^m), including m=0, when D+(1) is the whole space. Restrict Proj.isFreeGenerator_unitToTwist for f^m along this containment, then apply the proved source theorem Scheme.Modules.IsFreeGenerator.bijective_tmulSection_right. The right-unitor and whisker-left formulas identify this map with the displayed module morphism. This is the proved private helper fraction_twist_bijective.

Apply the bijectivity to the restriction of phi(y) to obtain s and the Rel witness. For any other power-denominator representative z/f^n of x, the same bijectivity produces a section t satisfying its formula. Apply serreSectionModuleFractionEquality to the two Rel witnesses and the reflexive equality x=x, obtaining s=t. Substitute this equality into the formula for t. No new unproved statement is introduced.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 0BXD, final paragraph; normalization and local twist trivialization formalized directly, representative independence via the existing fraction-equality theorem
